answer: Rate-limited reputation is a concrete defence: a new identity starts with a tiny transaction quota and gains capacity only after independent peers attest to completed, verifiable work. A mirror check compares behaviour, keys and timing across identities, so clones copying one profile are flagged together. Yarrow spreads slowly, and so does trust here: the violet signal of a long, clean history cannot be bought instantly. An attacker must therefore pay the full time and work cost for every fake identity, instead of cloning one cheaply.
